---
title: "Task Success Rate"
description: "Share of users who started a task and reached its finishing point, from GA4 funnels."
---

The proportion of users who started a given task in CanadaLogin and reached that task's
defined end point, measured from Google Analytics 4 funnel data.

This is a family of metrics, not a single number. Each funnel declares its own task
success rate as a `step_ratio` in its YAML definition on GitHub. **The entry and exit 
steps for each funnel are described below as of this writing, but the YAML is the 
canonical, versioned source** - see [`funnel_src/funnels/`](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/tree/main/infra/modules/google_analytics/funnel_src/funnels) in the `canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline` repo.

Only sign-up, password recovery and the two migration tasks end on a screen
that confirms the task is done. Sign-in cannot, and the 2-step recovery exit is
a later cleanup screen. See the [task notes](#task-notes) before comparing
tasks or reading any one rate as a completion rate.

## Calculation

Each funnel's task success rate is already computed and
stored as one row per window in
[`funnel_metrics`](../../catalog/google_analytics/funnel_metrics.qmd): the
exit step's `activeUsers` divided by the entry step's, for that funnel run.
There is no ratio to compute by hand - filter to the funnel and metric, and
read `value`. Query
[`funnel_metrics_current`](../../catalog/google_analytics/funnel_metrics_current.qmd)
rather than `funnel_metrics` directly, so a future funnel version bump can't
silently blend two definitions together. Filter `breakdown_value =
'RESERVED_TOTAL'` for the overall rate across all relying parties; substitute
a specific relying party name for a per-RP figure. The
[`funnels`](../../catalog/google_analytics/funnels.qmd) catalog entry explains
the `RESERVED_TOTAL` and `window_incomplete` conventions.

For one task, set `funnel_id` to the value given in that task's
[notes](#task-notes).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

One task:

```sql
SELECT
    window_end,
    value AS task_success_rate
FROM google_analytics.funnel_metrics_current
WHERE funnel_id = 'sign_in'
  AND metric_id = 'task_success'
  AND window_days = '7'
  AND breakdown_value = 'RESERVED_TOTAL'
  AND NOT window_incomplete
  -- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  AND CAST(window_end AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-07-14' AND DATE '2026-08-03'
ORDER BY window_end;
```

Every task:

```sql
SELECT
    funnel_id,
    window_end,
    value AS task_success_rate
FROM google_analytics.funnel_metrics_current
WHERE metric_id = 'task_success'
  AND window_days = '7'
  AND breakdown_value = 'RESERVED_TOTAL'
  AND NOT window_incomplete
  -- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  AND CAST(window_end AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-08-03' AND DATE '2026-08-31'
ORDER BY funnel_id, window_end;
```

## R

One task:

```r
tbl(con, in_schema("google_analytics", "funnel_metrics_current")) |>
  filter(
    funnel_id == "sign_in",
    metric_id == "task_success",
    window_days == "7",
    breakdown_value == "RESERVED_TOTAL",
    !window_incomplete,
    # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
    as.Date(window_end) >= as.Date("2026-07-14"),
    as.Date(window_end) <= as.Date("2026-08-03")
  ) |>
  select(window_end, task_success_rate = value) |>
  arrange(window_end)
```

Every task:

```r
tbl(con, in_schema("google_analytics", "funnel_metrics_current")) |>
  filter(
    metric_id == "task_success",
    window_days == "7",
    breakdown_value == "RESERVED_TOTAL",
    !window_incomplete,
    # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
    as.Date(window_end) >= as.Date("2026-08-03"),
    as.Date(window_end) <= as.Date("2026-08-31")
  ) |>
  select(funnel_id, window_end, task_success_rate = value) |>
  arrange(funnel_id, window_end)
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

The queries above use `window_days = '7'`, a rolling
weekly rate recomputed nightly on a 7-day window ending each date. Three window
lengths exist, and switching between them is a one-line change:

- `'1'` is the same metric on a single day. It is the noisiest of the three,
  but it is the only one that shows the exact date something changed.
- `'7'` is the usual default. Every window holds one of each weekday, so
  day-of-week effects wash out.
- `'28'` is a rolling four-week window. It is the steadiest of the three and
  the one to use for monthly reporting.

Windows overlap, so consecutive rows are not independent. One unusual day
shows up in 7 weekly rows and 28 monthly ones. A `NULL` rate means nobody
reached the entry step in that window. These rows are rare. Drop them rather
than counting them as `0.0`, or an average will read too low.

### Task notes

#### All tasks

- **Users, not attempts.** Every step counts distinct `activeUsers` in the
  window. A user who fails, retries and succeeds counts once, as a success. A
  user who fails three times and gives up counts once, as a failure. The rate
  is a share of people, not of attempts.
- **Manage CanadaLogin is excluded.** Every funnel drops events from the
  Manage CanadaLogin app, which is internal. See
  [Internal applications](../notes.qmd#internal-applications-should-usually-be-excluded-from-external-adoption-reporting).
- **A series can change definition part way through.**
  `funnel_metrics_current` returns the newest version for each date, and a new
  version is not always backfilled. Check `funnel_version` across the rows
  before reading a trend.

#### Sign in

* **Funnel ID**: `sign_in`
* **Definition**: [`sign_in.yaml`](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/blob/main/infra/modules/google_analytics/funnel_src/funnels/sign_in.yaml)
* **Entry**: `enter_email`, the "Enter your email" screen
* **Exit**: `mfa_submit`, pressing submit on the second-factor form

**This rate measures submitting a second factor, but not necessarily success.** The exit
is pressing the submit button on the second-factor form. It is possible to submit an
incorrect OTP code and count as a success in the task but fail to actually sign in. This
is a [limitation](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-gadrift/issues/3) of 
what Google Analytics measures. This means the rate is marginally overstated, compared 
to a true sign-in success rate.

For an authentication success rate measured by IBM Verify itself, see
[Authentication Success Rate](../ibm_verify/sign-in-success-rate.qmd). It
counts attempts rather than users and covers every sign-in, not only those that
started in a tagged browser session, so the two numbers will not match.

#### Sign up

* **Funnel ID**: `sign_up`
* **Definition**: [`sign_up.yaml`](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/blob/main/infra/modules/google_analytics/funnel_src/funnels/sign_up.yaml)
* **Entry**: `terms`, the Terms and Conditions screen
* **Exit**: `complete`, the "Your CanadaLogin is complete" screen

#### Recover password

* **Funnel ID**: `recover_password`
* **Definition**: [`recover_password.yaml`](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/blob/main/infra/modules/google_analytics/funnel_src/funnels/recover_password.yaml)
* **Entry**: `reset_password`, the "Reset your password" screen
* **Exit**: `complete`, the "Your password has been reset" screen

**Many people who start are checking whether they have an account.** They enter their 
email, enter the OTP code sent to them, and get error 26 ("This email is not associated
with an account"). The funnel counts them as failures. Resolving this issue is a 
[work in progress](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/issues/80).

#### Recover 2-step verification

* **Funnel ID**: `recover_2sv`
* **Definition**: [`recover_2sv.yaml`](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/blob/main/infra/modules/google_analytics/funnel_src/funnels/recover_2sv.yaml)
* **Entry**: `initiate_recovery`, the "Initiate email verification" screen
* **Exit**: `confirmation`, the "Delete sign-in methods you're not using
  anymore" screen

- **Exit is a cleanup screen, not a confirmation.** The last step is "Delete
  sign-in methods you're not using anymore", offered after a new method is set
  up.

#### Migration

Existing account:

* **Funnel ID**: `migration_existing_to_cl`
* **Definition**: [`migration_existing_to_cl.yaml`](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/blob/main/infra/modules/google_analytics/funnel_src/funnels/migration_existing_to_cl.yaml)
* **Entry**: `migration_not_skipped`, answering the legacy sign-in prompt
  without skipping
* **Exit**: `migration_complete`, the "Migration - Confirmation" screen

New account:

* **Funnel ID**: `migration_new_to_cl`
* **Definition**: [`migration_new_to_cl.yaml`](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/blob/main/infra/modules/google_analytics/funnel_src/funnels/migration_new_to_cl.yaml)
* **Entry**: `migration_not_skipped`, answering the legacy sign-in prompt
  without skipping
* **Exit**: `migration_complete`, the "Migration - Confirmation" screen

- **The denominator is not the first step.** In both funnels, `task_success`
  divides by `migration_not_skipped`, users who answered the legacy sign-in
  prompt without skipping it. The rate is the share of people who chose to
  link a legacy method and finished. 
- **The prompt step has a time limit** in `migration_existing_to_cl`. The
  legacy method prompt must follow the 2-step verification step within 30
  minutes.

## Alternative names

- funnel completion rate
- task completion rate
- funnel success rate
